correctness.rationale: Isomorphism-free leaf extension exhaustively generates 1,1,1,2,3,6,11,23,47 trees at sizes one through nine; matching enumeration recovers characteristic polynomials by the forest matching identity. For each of the four exact nine-vertex witnesses, the graph Chevalley–Eilenberg matrices have degree 0–4 rational ranks (0,8,75,404,1383), (0,8,75,404,1382), (0,8,73,397,1351), (0,8,73,397,1350); cochain dimensions are 1,17,136,680,2380,6188, so degree-four Betti numbers are 593,594 and 632,633. Differential squares vanish by derivation, and full finite chain checks pass. Exact Fraction row elimination, mod-prime comparison and Nomizu identify real de Rham Betti values. No claim of infinite extension or integral cohomology is made.

value.rationale: Adjacency spectrum and degree multiset are standard hard-to-distinguish graph invariants, while graph-associated nilmanifold Betti numbers are geometric invariants motivated by contemporary Poincare polynomial work. The exhaustive minimal pair classification and first separating fourth-degree coefficient constitute a natural quantitative boundary: degree-four de Rham topology distinguishes both exceptional collisions, whereas all lower Betti numbers coincide. This is a complete sharply scoped example, not a random cherry-picked number or mere restatement of isomorphism rigidity.
